title: Relative clauses with a preposition: the country they belonged to

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know relative clauses with a preposition and *el que* from B1 Unit 20. They are useful for talking about a nation: the country people belonged to, the community they lived in, the group they felt part of.

sections.title: Preposition + article + que
rows: la comunidad a la que pertenecen
el país en el que vivían
los grupos de los que formaban parte

items.spanish: El país al que pertenecían era nuevo.
items.english: The country they belonged to was new.

items.spanish: La comunidad a la que pertenecen es grande.
items.english: The community they belong to is large.

items.spanish: El país en el que gobernaban no tenía identidad común.
items.english: The country in which they governed had no common identity.

items.spanish: Los grupos de los que formaban parte eran pequeños.
items.english: The groups they were part of were small.

sections.content: The article agrees with the noun you describe (*el país*, *la comunidad*, *los grupos*), and the preposition is the one the verb needs: *pertenecer a*, *vivir en*, *formar parte de*. Never leave it out: not *el país que pertenecían*.
